subject: a short, sturdy African American woman with a warm, determined face, dark eyes and dark hair swept up neatly on top of her head

panels.01-delta: cotton fields on a Louisiana plantation near the Mississippi River in winter 1867, a small weathered wooden cabin with smoke rising from its chimney, bare trees, a wide grey river in the distance, quiet wide establishing shot, a family's first child born free, post-Civil War American South
panels.02-washtub: a younger {S} in a plain cotton work dress and apron, sleeves rolled up, scrubbing laundry in a large wooden washtub in a crowded St. Louis backyard in 1888, lines of white sheets drying overhead, a little girl of three sitting on the steps beside her, steam and morning light, tired but resolute
panels.03-hair-grower: {S} in a simple dark skirt and white blouse standing at a kitchen table in a small Denver rented room in 1905, carefully stirring an ointment in a pot and filling small round tins, glass jars, a scale and handwritten notes on the table, lamplight, focused and hopeful, her own product taking shape
panels.04-door-to-door: {S} in a long dark travelling dress and hat, carrying a leather sample case, showing small round tins to a group of Black women on the front porch of a wooden house in a small Southern town in 1906, dusty road, picket fence, sunlight, friendly demonstration and conversation
panels.05-lelia-college: {S} in an elegant high-collared white blouse and long dark skirt teaching a class of young African American women in a bright beauty training parlour in Pittsburgh in 1908, students in white aprons practising on each other's hair at a row of chairs, a mirror and basins, pride and learning
panels.06-factory: {S} in a tailored dark suit and white blouse walking through her busy factory floor in Indianapolis around 1910, rows of African American women workers in white aprons filling and labelling small round tins at long wooden tables, big windows, crates ready for shipping, a woman manager with a ledger beside her, industry and purpose
panels.07-floor: {S} in a fine dark dress with a high lace collar rising from her seat in the audience of a crowded convention hall in Chicago in 1912, speaking with confidence, rows of men in dark suits turning in their chairs to look at her in surprise, a speakers' platform in the background, tall windows with summer light, courage and dignity, no text
panels.08-agents: {S} in an elegant dark gown standing at a podium before a large hall filled with about two hundred well-dressed African American women agents in 1917 Philadelphia, some holding certificates and flowers, an American flag and plain bunting behind her, warm light, a proud and hopeful gathering, no text, no letters
